cards.text: Jesus promised His apostles power when the Holy Spirit comes on them (Acts 1:8). Now the day of Pentecost comes, and Jesus' followers are all together in one place. ALL of them, same place, same time? Friend, I have seen group chats that couldn't agree on a time for a WEEK.

cards.question: Suddenly a sound like a mighty rushing wind fills the whole house where Jesus' followers are sitting. Where does that sound come from?
Jesus' followers see tongues like flames of fire, which separate and come to rest on each one of them.
Then Jesus' followers in that house are all filled with something. What is it?

cards.text: And they begin to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit enables them. Me? Years in a junk drawer, and the only other language I ever picked up was Dead Battery.
Now, Jerusalem has God-fearing Jews living there from every nation under heaven. EVERY nation, friend, which is a whole lot of different ways to say "good morning."

cards.question: When the sound rings out, a crowd comes together in bewilderment, because each one hears Jesus' followers speaking his own ___.

cards.text: Astounded and amazed, the crowd asks: aren't these speakers all Galileans, so how is each of us hearing them in his own native language? I can hear it now: WAIT, run that back.

Then the crowd runs down where they're all from: Parthians, Medes, Elamites, folks from Mesopotamia to Egypt, visitors from Rome, both Jews and converts to Judaism, Cretans and Arabs. Friend, that is the BIGGEST round of where-are-you-from I have ever heard.

cards.question: In all those languages, the crowd hears these Spirit-filled Galileans telling about the wonders of ___.
Once they hear Jesus' followers speaking, the whole crowd understands right away what it all means.

cards.text: But others in that crowd start mocking them. There's ALWAYS one table in the back that thinks it's funnier than the show.

cards.question: What do the mockers in the crowd say about Jesus' followers?

answers.text: They are drunk on new wine

cards.text: Hang on to your apron, friend, because this story is NOT done.
